owner: CC owns the retirement mechanics. Akien owns the design decision that corrections-as-training-data replaces approve/disprove.
state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> [PROVED] (PROVED 2026-08-29: retirement note on bin/cmd/recordverdict naming cairn review. Retirement field on recordverdict-cli-door ticket. No gate reads approve/disprove binary. Proof green x2, sealed netns. Verdict answers chart 3/3.)
intention: Retire `cairn recordverdict` — the approve/disprove adjudication model is replaced by `cairn review`, where corrections carry the training data as words, not a binary signal.
why: Akien, 2026-08-28: 'recordverdict will become obsolete. the approve/disprove adjudication is the old way. now we do artifact approvals — things just are clear or they go back to design with why it got booted back. even on approvals, i can't just approve or disapprove, i have to spell out the whys. the training data is the corrections themselves, not a binary signal.'
traces_to: Law 1 — a binary signal (approve/disprove) forces re-derivation of WHY something was approved or disproved; the correction itself IS the training data.
CP3 — a binary signal strips the why, making it unfalsifiable; words carry the falsifiable content.

how.cli_retirement: Mark bin/cmd/recordverdict with a retirement note pointing at cairn review as the successor. The command stays on disk (established pattern from chart and ground-loop retirements).
how.ticket_retirement: Add a retirement field to tickets/recordverdict-cli-door.json naming cairn review as the successor, the date, and Akien's reason. The PROVED state is preserved.
how.primitive_scope: The learning_block.record_verdict primitive is NOT retired by this ticket. The skilldial still reads its match_rate (approvals/disproves ratio). The CLI retires now; the primitive retires when the dial migrates to a new signal source. Two retirements, sequenced.

gates: code-seam invariant: proved + feeds-back-on-failure. PROVE GATE: the command carries a retirement note, cairn review is named as successor, no gate reads approve/disprove for crossing decisions. FEEDS BACK: a red names what still depends on the binary signal.
falsifier: DONE when recordverdict is marked retired with cairn review named as successor, and no live workflow depends on the approve/disprove binary for gate passage. WRONG INTENT if the retirement breaks the dial (it shouldn't — the CLI retires, the primitive stays), or if cairn review's corrections don't carry the training data Akien described.
horizon: Small — the retirement is a file edit (retirement field on the ticket, retirement note on the command), not a code change.
dependencies: bin/cmd/review — the successor, already built and operational.
cairn/machines/learning_block/learning_block.py — the primitive that stays; only the CLI retires.
distinctions_recorded: CLI RETIRES, PRIMITIVE STAYS: cairn recordverdict (the CLI face) retires. learning_block.record_verdict (the primitive) stays until the dial migrates. Two retirements, sequenced.

BINARY SIGNAL vs CORRECTIONS-AS-DATA: recordverdict captured approve/disprove + verbatim — the binary was the signal, words were metadata. cairn review captures words as the signal. The inversion is the design shift.
RETIREMENT IS LIFECYCLE, NOT FAILURE: recordverdict-cli-door (PROVED) was correct when built. The design moved on. The proof was valid; the need changed.
provenance: Born from idea 2026-08-28-recordverdict-will-become-obsolete-the-approve-d (Akien: 'the approve/disprove adjudication is the old way'). Ticketed 2026-08-29.
watchme: none — the retirement is a one-time state change. cairn review's efficacy is monitored by the skill_block's dial (skilldial.py). The proof at bin/proofs/test_cairn_command.py covers the command.
